companies.planMenu.featureGuide.detailsS: Guide: what a feature is, fields, menu, plans, anchors, and catalog refactor
companies.planMenu.featureGuide.lead: Read this before bulk-deleting definitions. The Description column comes from the database (editable); the gray hint summarizes typical usage for each code.
companies.planMenu.featureGuide.blockCon:
A feature definition is the unit the product includes or excludes per commercial plan (module, form, quota, or integration). Backend and billing rely on the same catalog you see here.

Example: if the Professional plan includes INVENTORY, tenants on that plan are entitled to the inventory module according to app rules.
companies.planMenu.featureGuide.blockFie:
Code: stable identifier (USERS, INVENTORY); do not change it to avoid breaking integrations.

Name and description: admin-facing text; description can spell out quotas or screens.

Kind: Module (large area), Form (specific screen/flow), Quota (numeric consumption), Integration (API or other channel).

Measured/consumable: when enabled, usage can be tracked per period.

Technical anchor (resource ref): key that ties the definition to menu and permissions (see Anchors).
companies.planMenu.featureGuide.blockMen:
Each menu row can link to a definition in two ways: (1) explicit link saved in the database (Apply link), or (2) automatic match when the item permission or route fits the resource ref or feature code.

Example: an item with permissionKey "ventas.customers.view" matches a feature whose resource ref is exactly "ventas.customers.view" or the prefix "ventas.customers".
companies.planMenu.featureGuide.blockPla:
Pick a plan above and use Add to plan / Remove from plan on menu rows or on unlinked definitions. Changes are draft until Save plan, which persists to saas_plan_features.

Example: removing PAYROLL from the Starter plan hides payroll for subscriptions assigned to that plan (depending on how the app reads the catalog).
companies.planMenu.featureGuide.blockAnc:
Exact permission: "inventario.products.view" matches a menu item with that permissionKey.

Permission prefix: "ventas.customers" matches any permission starting with ventas.customers.

Route: "/inventario/productos" or a suffix that matches the menu route.

Module: if the anchor is "inventario" and the item has moduleKey inventario and a permission under that tree, it may match.

If the anchor is empty, the system may infer from the feature code (e.g. INVENTORY → inventario…); prefer an explicit anchor for new screens.
companies.planMenu.featureGuide.blockCod:
USERS: active user seats per tenant (often metered). DOCUMENTS: commercial documents with optional per-period limits. INVENTORY / ACCOUNTING / PAYROLL: whole modules. API_ACCESS: programmatic access. CUSTOMERS: sales/customers. BRANCHES: branches/locations.

INVENTARIO_TARIFFS, INVENTARIO_CATEGORIES, ACCESS_PROFILES: specific forms/areas added by migrations; usually align with inventory or security routes/permissions.

Use the per-row hint column for a short usage summary.
companies.planMenu.featureGuide.blockRef:
There is no global reset button: deleting definitions is destructive (removes plan rows, overrides, usage, and menu links).

Recommended in a test environment: (1) export or note which plans included each feature; (2) delete only definitions you will recreate; (3) create new definitions via Super Admin or API; (4) re-include features on each plan and save; (5) re-link menu items.

In production avoid deleting standard codes; prefer editing name, description, and anchor to fix menu alignment.

1) The company subscribes to a commercial plan: that plan defines what the subscription includes (modules, screens/forms, and other SaaS definitions linked to the plan).

3) Use the catalog below: blue badge = included in the plan; green badge = product module is effectively enabled for the tenant (server state, read-only here).
